title: God of All Consolation, Take
description: God of All Consolation, Take in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 12 verses and a piano.
about: John Wesley printed these words in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 537. They first appeared in a book he and his brother Charles published together, and the Collection's own index cannot say which of the two wrote them.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Common Metre (8.6.8.6), and this page sets them to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: God of all con-sol-a-tion, take The glo-ry of thy grace! Thy gifts to thee we ren-der back In cease-less songs of praise.

lines: God of all consolation, take
The glory of thy grace!
Thy gifts to thee we render back
In ceaseless songs of praise.
Through thee we now together came,
In singleness of heart;
We met, O Jesus, in thy name,
And in thy name we part.
We part in body, not in mind,
Our minds continue one;
And, each to each in Jesus joined,
We hand in hand go on.
Subsists as in us all one soul,
No power can make us twain;
And mountains rise and oceans roll
To sever us, in vain.
Present we still in spirit are,
And intimately nigh,
While on the wings of faith and prayer
We each to other fly.
Our life is hid with Christ in God;
Our Life shall soon appear,
And shed his glory all abroad
In all his members here.
The heavenly treasure now we have
In a vile house of clay;
But he shall to the utmost save,
And keep it to that day.
Our souls are in his mighty hand,
And he shall keep them still;
And you and I shall surely stand
With him on Zion's hill!
Him eye to eye we there shall see,
Our face like his shall shine:
O what a glorious company,
When saints and angels join!
O what a joyful meeting there!
In robes of white arrayed,
Palms in our hands we all shall bear,
And crowns upon our head.
Then let us lawfully contend,
And fight our passage through;
Bear in our faithful minds the end,
And keep the prize in view.
Then let us hasten to the day
When all shall be brought home;
Come, O Redeemer, come away,
O Jesus, quickly come!

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788; John Wesley died in 1791.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788) or John Wesley (1703–1791), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
